item.title: A fully bilingual Crypt
item.description:
The Crypt now speaks English and French everywhere official, with a language question for new members and /announce for bilingual announcements.

The Crypt has had a French section since day one, but most of the server still spoke English first. With Crypt Keeper v1.1.0, the whole Crypt is bilingual.

English first, French underneath

Everything official now carries both languages, English on top and French on its own line under it: the rules, the links, the welcome message, birthday posts and announcements. The three official channels got bilingual names too: #rules-règles, #announcements-annonces and #links-liens, and the shared channels have a French line in their description.

Pick your language

Onboarding now starts with Language · Langue: English, Français or both. It gives the new Anglophone role, the Francophone role, or both. Members with both get their welcome and birthday messages in both languages.

Chat in whichever you like

The main channels are shared, so write in the language you're comfortable with. The ⚜️ Section francophone is still there for people who want a French-only corner.

/announce

Announcements from me now go through /announce: a form with English and French fields that posts one message with both, with an optional ping.

Updating without a rebuild

For the existing server this arrived as a /update-server step. It only renames and rewords channels that still had their original names and descriptions, edits Crypt Keeper's own rules and links posts in place, and leaves everything changed by hand exactly as it was.

item.title: The Crypt SMP gets a home in the Crypt
item.description:
The Minecraft server now has its own section in the same Discord, with news, how to join, chat, and support tickets for in-game problems.

The Crypt SMP is my own Minecraft server, and I didn't want a second Discord just for it. So it now lives inside the Crypt, in its own ⛏️ The Crypt SMP section. Crypt Keeper v1.1.0 builds and runs it.

Who sees what

  • News and how to join are open to everyone, read-only, so anybody can see what the server is about and how to connect.
  • Chat, suggestions, screenshots and a voice channel are for members with the new Crypt SMP role. Pick it in onboarding or under Channels & Roles.

Everything in the section is bilingual, English first and French underneath, like the rest of the Crypt.

Support tickets, for Minecraft only

The support channel has four buttons: help, bug report, report a player and ban appeal. Press one, fill in your Minecraft name and what happened, and Crypt Keeper opens a private ticket that only you and the moderators can see. Press Close when it's sorted. You can have one open ticket at a time.

Tickets exist only for the Minecraft server. Anything else in the Crypt still goes to a moderator by direct message, and the older posts that mentioned tickets were cleaned up.

The server address

The how-to-join post shows the Java and Bedrock addresses and the version, and I update it with a single command whenever something changes.

Join the Crypt to see it.

item.title: Game deals: Steam only, with an Open in Steam button
item.description:
Crypt Keeper's game deals now post only Steam games, and every post has a button that opens the game's Steam page.

Crypt Keeper posts the best PC game deals in the Crypt. Two small changes in v1.4.1 and v1.4.2 make those posts easier to use.

An Open in Steam button

Every deal post now has an Open in Steam button under it. One tap and you're on the game's store page, ready to buy. The same button is on the DM you get when a game on your /wishlist drops to your price.

Steam only, for now

Deals used to come from several stores, and not every one could link straight to the game. For now Crypt Keeper only posts Steam deals, and only for games that have a Steam ID, so every post opens the real Steam page. Epic, GOG, Humble and the other stores are paused. I can switch them back on later with a single setting.

What did not change

  • The filters are the same: a minimum discount, a maximum price and a minimum Steam rating, set by staff with /deals filters.
  • /deal, /wishlist, the deal ping roles and the big sales calendar all work as before.

Want a ping for deals? Press the 🔔 button under any deal, or use /deal-pings. Join the Crypt to see it.

item.title: Crypt Keeper posts the devlog, and gets /update-server
item.description:
Every new devlog post now shows up in the Crypt by itself, in English and French, in a new #devlog channel.

Crypt Keeper, the Crypt's own bot, learned a new trick. It checks this site's devlog every 30 minutes, and each new post lands in #devlog on the Discord server, with its title, a one-line summary in English and French, and links to both versions.

The channel is read-only, so the updates stay easy to follow. Talk about them in the usual channels.

/update-server

New features that need something on the server now arrive as small updates. /update-server lists only what's new, explains each change and waits for an Apply click. Each update runs once and touches only its own new thing, so anything changed by hand in Discord stays exactly as it is. No more running the full /build-server again.

The devlog now covers everything: this website, the Discord server and Crypt Keeper, the Minecraft server, the homelab and the setup. So #devlog is the one place to see what changed.

item.title: Stavo on the homelab page, and one devlog for everything
item.description:
The homelab page now shows Stavo, my friend Ronniie's self-hosted platform, and this devlog now covers every project, with a filter.

Stavo, by a friend

The homelab page has a new section about Stavo, the self-hosted platform my good friend Ronniie builds at NullDaily. It runs on your own hardware: files, photos, notes, game servers, hosting and billing, status pages, passwords, mail and more. A lot of my lab might end up running on it, so each app I'm watching has a card that links to it.

One devlog for everything

This devlog now covers every project, not just the website: the Discord server and Crypt Keeper, the Minecraft server, the homelab and the setup. Each post says which project it's about, and the buttons above the list show only one project at a time. New posts also land in #devlog on the Discord server by themselves.

Cleaned up

The drawing of the next server is gone from the homelab page. The build plan and the reasons behind it are still there.

item.title: Every time in your own time zone
item.description:
Dates and times posted in the Crypt now show in each person's own time zone, and /timestamp makes them for anyone.

Half the Crypt is in Quebec and the rest is all over the place, so "9 PM" never meant the same thing for everyone. Not anymore.

  • Everything Crypt Keeper posts with a date (game nights, big sales, free games, deals) now uses Discord timestamps: Discord shows the time in your own time zone, and can count down to it.
  • /timestamp turns something like fri 9pm or 2026-10-31 19:00 into a code you can paste into any message. Everyone reading it sees their own local time.

Announcements from me will use them too, so you never have to convert from Eastern time again.

item.title: Version 1.0.0 of everything
item.description:
The website and Crypt Keeper now have real version numbers and builds, starting at v1.0.0, and every update from now on gets one.

Everything I build now has a version number, starting today at v1.0.0 for both this website and Crypt Keeper. The Minecraft server will get the same treatment when it's ready.

How to read a version

Versions look like v1.2.0 · build b66769c:

  • The last number goes up for fixes and small changes.
  • The middle number goes up for new features.
  • The first number goes up when something big changes and you'd want to know before updating.
  • The build is the exact change on GitHub it came from, so two copies of the same version can always be told apart.

Where you'll see it

  • At the bottom of every page of this site, linking to the changelog and the exact build on GitHub.
  • In Crypt Keeper's /bot version, its update button and its startup message.
  • On each devlog post and its announcement in #devlog, which list the versions it covers.
  • As releases with notes on GitHub, and in each project's changelog.

item.title: The site moved to GitHub, and learned French
item.description:
Every change now goes live on its own, the whole site is bilingual, and there are a few secrets to find.

Until now, updating this site meant zipping a folder and dragging it into Cloudflare. Not anymore. The site lives on GitHub, and every change pushed there is live about a minute later. Every version is kept, so any mistake is one click from undone.

En français aussi

A good part of my friends are French Canadian, so the whole site now exists in standard French. The FR button in the menu switches to the same page in the other language.

Things to find

  • Press the ` key for a terminal. Try neofetch.
  • Type the word crypt anywhere on the site.
  • There are achievements, tracked by the trophy in the footer.
  • The homelab page has a live map of how everything connects.

item.title: Welcome to The Crypt
item.description:
My Discord server is open, and it has its own custom bot: Crypt Keeper.

The Crypt is my Discord server: a hangout for friends, a place to find people to play with, and a corner for homelab and tech help. It has a full French section too.

Crypt Keeper

Instead of stacking five public bots, the server runs one custom bot written for it. Crypt Keeper builds the whole server layout in one command, welcomes new members with a banner, and keeps a message log for the staff.

  • Levels with six crypt-themed ranks, from Lost Soul to Crypt Legend.
  • Temporary voice rooms, game nights and a looking-for-group board.
  • Birthdays with their own cards, a question of the day and a weekly recap.
  • Free game alerts, trivia and a starboard for the best messages.
  • A first answer from AI on tech-help posts, with a daily limit to keep costs sane.

The server icon even follows the calendar: Halloween in October, Christmas in December, and a few special days in between. This website now does the same.

Join the Crypt if any of that sounds like your kind of place.

item.title: The site goes live
item.description:
tehzombijesus.ca is up: a link hub and portfolio, hosted on Cloudflare Pages.

For years "TehZombiJesus" has been a username on a dozen platforms and nothing that tied them together. Now there's a home base: tehzombijesus.ca.

It started as a simple link hub and grew into four pages: the homelab, the gaming setup I'm planning, the Ruenix Minecraft network, and the usual about me. It's plain HTML and CSS on Cloudflare Pages. No framework, no build step, nothing to update every week.

Locked down from day one

Security headers came before anything fancy. The site scores A+ on securityheaders.com: a strict content security policy, HSTS, no framing, and only the browser features the site actually needs. Every script runs from this domain, so nothing loads from somewhere I don't control.

The rest of this devlog is where the site, the server and the setup get built in public.
